text: Acme Global Systems Infrastructure and Operations Handbook Version 2.4. Section 1. Overview and Core Architecture. Acme Global maintains multi-region Kubernetes clusters across primary-us-east and secondary-eu-west regions. All production database instances utilize PostgreSQL 16 with streaming replication and asynchronous hot standby failover. The recovery point objective (RPO) for critical tier-1 transactional workloads is strictly 5 minutes, and the recovery time objective (RTO) is 15 minutes. In contrast, non-critical analytical databases operate with a relaxed recovery point objective (RPO) of 24 hours. The standard server operating system is Debian 12 with mandatory kernel hardening enabled across all worker nodes. Acme Global Systems Infrastructure Operations Handbook Version 2.4. Section 2. Backup and Disaster Recovery Procedures. Production database snapshots must be taken every 6 hours and retained for 30 calendar days in encrypted object storage. All database snapshots must be encrypted using customer-managed AWS KMS keys with annual key rotation mandated. In the event of a catastrophic regional failure, automatic DNS failover triggers within 120 seconds, routing traffic to eu-west hot standby. Staging and development environments do not receive automated failover and their snapshots are retained for only 7 calendar days. Disaster recovery recovery drills must be executed semi-annually with documented sign-off from the SRE Lead.

Acme Enterprise Data Mesh Product Specification Version 1.0. Section 1. Ingestion Pipelines and Rate Limits. The Data Mesh ingestion API processes incoming telemetry events via gRPC and HTTPS endpoints. The standard ingestion rate limit is 10000 events per second per tenant organization, with burst allowance up to 15000 events per second for a maximum duration of 60 seconds. Payload sizes exceeding 2 megabytes are rejected immediately with HTTP 413 Payload Too Large. Telemetry events with missing tenant headers are routed directly to the dead-letter queue (DLQ) for manual inspection within 24 hours. Acme Enterprise Data Mesh Product Specification Version 1.0. Section 2. Data Retention, Quotas, and Storage Tiers. Standard tenant telemetry is retained in hot memory-cached storage for 7 days before automated tiering to cold parquet archives for 365 days. However, database snapshots mentioned in infrastructure handbooks are managed independently of the telemetry mesh and adhere to 30-day storage limits. Under no circumstances does the Data Mesh retain uncompressed event streams for longer than 48 hours without tiering. Tenants requesting custom retention periods exceeding 365 days must purchase enterprise archive licenses.

Acme Corporation Information Security and Access Control Policy Version 4.1. Section 1. Identity, Authentication, and Password Standards. All Acme personnel and service contractors must authenticate using hardware security key FIDO2 multi-factor authentication (MFA). User passwords must be at least 16 characters in length containing uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special symbol characters. Service accounts are strictly prohibited from using static passwords and must authenticate exclusively via short-lived OAuth2 mTLS certificates expiring every 12 hours. Failed login attempts exceeding 5 consecutive trials trigger an automated 30-minute account lockout and notify the Security Operations Center (SOC). Acme Corporation Information Security and Access Control Policy Version 4.1. Section 2. Cryptographic Key Management and Access Revocation. Cryptographic service keys and TLS certificates must be rotated at least every 90 days without exception. In contrast, personnel access credentials and role assignments must undergo quarterly access review by designated department leads. Upon employee termination, automated access deprovisioning triggers immediately and must revoke all Active Directory and cloud IAM permissions within 60 seconds. Third-party contractor credentials expire automatically after 30 days unless an extension is approved in writing by the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).
